name: QQQ Condor — 3% of VAR
description: Size the wing to the account. Exit once the loss, net of the week's credit, reaches 3% of Monday net worth.
rebalance: weekly, Monday open to Friday close

data_source.label: Yahoo Finance free daily prices
data_source.banner: Modelled option prices, not a tape of fills. QQQ open, high, low, and close are Yahoo's split-adjusted bars. Implied vol is ^VXN, or ^VIX scaled by the median VXN/VIX ratio when ^VXN is missing. Strikes, credits, and stops are Black–Scholes with a flat strike skew, a spot-vol add-on on stop marks, and a bid/ask haircut. This book does not select a stock universe. SPY is a reference line only.

universe.note: Single ETF. Option prices are modelled from QQQ and VXN.

caveats: Modelled option prices, not a tape of fills. QQQ open, high, low, and close are Yahoo's split-adjusted bars. Implied vol is ^VXN, or ^VIX scaled by the median VXN/VIX ratio when ^VXN is missing. Strikes, credits, and stops are Black–Scholes with a flat strike skew, a spot-vol add-on on stop marks, and a bid/ask haircut. This book does not select a stock universe. SPY is a reference line only.
Size the wing to the account. Exit once the loss, net of the week's credit, reaches 3% of Monday net worth.
VAR for the 3% eject is Monday net worth. The loss is cost to close minus the total credit collected that week. Confirm that definition before treating the path as the live rule.

No historical option chain is used. Debits and credits are Black–Scholes mids with a half-spread of max($0.035, 10% of mid) per leg. That floor is the one that lines the 0.03-delta credit up with the recorded credits.
Intraday implied vol is not observed. Stop marks take the prior VXN and add 1.5 vol points per 1% spot drop, capped at 25 points.

VXN/VIX median scale is 1.214. 473 sessions in the window have no VXN print and use scaled VIX. 340 of 1441 weeks collect a positive put credit after the haircut. A 10-point wing on a low QQQ price usually does not.
A 10-point wing on early QQQ prices is a large fraction of spot, so the long wing is almost free and the position is close to a naked short with a far stop.
The entry is the week's first session, usually Monday, at the open. The same day's high and low can stop the new position. That open is not a gap fill.
From the next morning on, a stop that the open has already crossed fills at the open debit, capped at the wing. The loss can be much larger than 3% of VAR.
Equity is floored at one cent if a liquidation would have wiped the account, so the CAGR can still be computed. The trade row keeps the uncapped loss. Ruin is flagged.
Hypothetical dollars in the trade table are the model's P&L on a $10,000 or $200,000 account. Recorded fills are stored only as a percent of spot.
Commission is $0.65 per contract per leg on the entry and on a stop. Expiry pays no commission. Cash earns zero.
warnings: The $200k book filled 4 stops at the open because the open was already through the stop.

metrics.sharpe_basis: annualized daily simple returns, rf=0, 252-day year

verdict.title: The modelled condor does not clear its own costs.
verdict.edge: Held to Friday at desk size, the average week is -0.32% of the account (76.5% of weeks finish green, average win 0.04%, average loss -1.52%). The 2× credit stop averages -0.18% a week. 340 of 340 $10,000 trades buy back the same day, because the cost to close at the entry open is already about 4.7× the credit just received.
verdict.kills: On the 3% VAR book the wing's maximum loss is about the whole account. A stop that fills at the level loses 3% net of the credit. 4 opens on the $200,000 book were already through that level and filled at the open. The worst of those is -7.0% of the account. The book’s maximum drawdown is -99.5%.
verdict.sizing: Desk size risks 18.75% of Monday net worth (the 12.5% base VAR times the 1.5 edge cap) and cannot lose more than about one wing in a week. Filtering FOMC, CPI, short weeks, and 2% gaps puts the $10,000 3% book at -8.2% CAGR and -90.4% max drawdown, next to -8.2% and -90.5% unfiltered. On weeks since 2020, the modelled price to close the breached vertical at an intraday 3% stop has median $0.28 against the $0.65 figure. That is 0.44× the figure, $0.37 under it. The full sample median is $0.28. Matching $0.65 with this credit and this residual value on the safe side would mean a wing of about 44% of the account. This book sizes the wing to the whole account.

assumptions: VAR is the account's net worth at the Monday entry. The 3% loss is 3% of that number. This is the sizing plan's definition, and it is an assumption to confirm.
The loss is net of the premium collected that week: cost to close the whole condor, minus the total credit received. Commissions sit on top of that and are not part of the 3% test.
The tracking notes put that same 3% loss at roughly a 0.65 price to close the breached vertical. The model does not aim at 0.65. The calibration block reports the debit it produces.

The traded strike is the 0.03 delta. 0.025 and 0.02 are reconciliation columns only. Delta is Black–Scholes with T equal to the calendar days from entry to the last session, divided by 365, r = 4%, q = 0, sigma = the prior session's VXN.

The short strike is rounded to the nearest dollar. The long strike is 10 points further out. The sheet has no long strike. Ten points is the calculator's width. On a $40 QQQ that wing is very wide and the long is nearly worthless.
A put credit at or below zero skips the week. A call credit at or below zero drops the call and trades the put spread.

The half-spread charged on every leg is the larger of $0.035 and 10% of the mid. The short is sold at the bid and bought back at the ask. Settlement at expiry is intrinsic, with no commission. A stop pays commission on the way out. The floor was set so the modelled 0.03-delta credits land near the recorded credits.
Commission is $0.65 per contract per leg. Cash earns nothing. Early assignment is ignored.

Strike skew versus VXN is flat. A positive put skew was checked against the recorded credits and made the model too rich. Stop marks still add vol when spot has moved since the prior close: 1.5 vol points per 1% drop (cap 25) and 0.4 per 1% rise (cap 10). That intraday vol is not observed.
Close marks use that session's VXN. Entry and stop marks use the prior session's VXN plus the spot-vol add-on. Before VXN exists, vol is VIX times the median VXN/VIX ratio.

The entry open is not treated as a gap through the stop. From the next session on, an open already through the stop fills at the open, capped at the wing. An intraday breach fills at the stop. The adverse mark is the worse of the low and the high. Both extremes are not added together.
Friday intraday marks keep a quarter-day of residual time. The close, if the stop has not fired, is the intrinsic value.

The desk books risk 18.75% of Monday net worth. The 3% books set contracts so the wing's maximum loss is about the whole account. One contract is the minimum. A book that cannot buy one contract skips the week.

The filtered book skips a week with fewer than five sessions, a Monday (or first-session) gap of 2% or more in either direction, a week that contains an FOMC announcement (or the Sunday before a Monday entry), or a CPI release. The first matching reason is the one counted.

The 2.90-sigma floor in the calculator is a stricter strike than 0.03 delta and is not the strike this sheet traded. Earnings windows and the calculator's call-block on a down Monday are notes, not filters, except for the explicit 2% gap on the filtered book.

CPI dates other than 2024 were compiled. A one-day miss usually stays inside the same week. Gate 1 (the live IV versus VXN check) cannot be rebuilt from daily bars; recorded fill IV sits close to VXN.
rules: Sell the 0.03-delta condor at the Monday open and hold it to the Friday intrinsic settlement.
Same entry. Buy the condor back once the cost to close reaches twice the credit collected.
Size the wing to the account. Exit once the loss, net of the week's credit, reaches 3% of Monday net worth.
The 3% VAR book, skipping holiday-short weeks, 2% Monday gaps, FOMC weeks, and CPI weeks.
lessons: The bust notes keep coming back to the open: large gaps in either direction, not a slow grind through the short strike.
FOMC weeks and CPI mornings cluster on both the put side and the call side. A CPI print on the Friday before an FOMC week is named more than once.
Holiday-short weeks are described as fussy on both sides. The filtered book drops any week with fewer than five sessions.
A second week of a sharp bounce, debt-ceiling noise, and single-name earnings show up in the notes. Several notes say the headline was not really the cause.
One call-side note in August 2026 records a stop-out on a gap two days into the week. That is the overnight case the 3% book fills at the open.
The sheet's 2.90-sigma distance would have sat further out of the money than the 0.03 delta that was actually marked. This backtest follows the marked delta.

bust.definition: A bust is the last session's close beyond the short strike. The sheet's counts use the unrounded 0.03 / 0.025 / 0.02 strikes.

sheet.note: Counts taken from the tracking sheet: put busts 4.00% / 3.76% / 3.06% and call busts 2.70% / 2.24% / 1.65% at 0.03 / 0.025 / 0.02 delta.

recorded.note: Credits are a fraction of the Monday open. The model/recorded ratio divides the modelled vertical credit by the recorded vertical credit. No contract counts and no dollar fills are stored.

trigger.note: Stop fills are the weeks closed at a 3% VAR loss during the session. The tested vertical is the breached side's debit, after the bid/ask haircut, at the spot where the condor loss equals 3% of Monday net worth. Gap fills are left out of the median. The since-2020 block is the comparison to the $0.65 figure, because that is when a 10-point wing and the credits look like the recent book.

live.note: Each return_pct is that week alone on a fresh hypothetical $200,000 account under the 3% VAR rule. It is a fraction of Monday net worth. The compounded path of the full backtest is a separate book and is not reused here. Null means the model collected no credit that week.
